The United States Space Force (USSF) at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base is searching for a Modeling & Simulation Production Manager to support the National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC), (GG-0132-13). This position is covered by the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS).

For additional information about DCIPS, click here: https://dcips.defense.gov/ Description: Are you a dynamic, high-caliber, technical production manager ready to safeguard critical intelligence and directly shape the nation's security?

The National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC) is the US Space Force's premier authority on foreign space capabilities and threats. We deliver game-changing, predictive scientific and technical intelligence (S&TI) that empowers joint force warfighters, national leaders, and defense acquisition professionals.

As we rapidly scale our mission capabilities, we are seeking a proactive, visionary Production Manager to pave the way. In this high-impact role, you will work in tandem with NSIC squadrons that drive our Modeling & Simulation (M&S) production planning and prioritization framework.

You will become a trusted mission partner at the forefront of space intelligence, coordinating internally and externally with influential agencies such as Space Systems Command (SSC) and the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA). If you are an articulate results-driven professional, your next mission starts here.

Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate is a proactive, systems-thinking professional who operates effectively at the critical intersection of threat intelligence analysis (Red) and operational capabilities (Blue).

Beyond traditional production management, you will serve as a vital Mission Integrator possessing deep space domain familiarity and the technical acumen required to prioritize sophisticated Modeling & Simulation (M&S) frameworks.

You will work in tandem with the model-producing squadrons to manage requests, prioritize production, and provide production progress transparency.

You will stand out if you have the ability to work independently; plan, organize, manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines and expertly oversee joint production and federation plans while actively connecting and engaging with committee members.

Bringing a blend of expertise involving fundamental Modeling & Simulation knowledge, governance, standardization, and a self-motivated drive to build bridges across NSIC, external modeling agencies, and the intelligence and defense communities is also highly desirable Key Areas of Expertise - Proven track record of aligning diverse mission partners around common operational goals and fostering interagency cooperation, overseeing joint production and federation plans, and actively connecting and engaging with committee members. - Proven ability to define, translate, and implement complex M&S governance and standards established by the broader USSF enterprise, ensuring our frameworks remain aligned and compliant.

Experienced with friendly force ("Blue") and/or threat (Red) modeling architecture and requirements, methodologies such as Signature and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) principles - Experienced in directly translating complex technical requirements into actionable production needs. - Possess a strong working knowledge of the operational structure and mission areas of the United States Space Force (USSF), paired with a deep understanding of the NSIC M&S mission set. - Possess exceptional executive presence with demonstrated experience briefing and advising DoW senior leadership and senior civilian counterparts. - Ability to operate with high autonomy in fast-paced environments-effectively prioritizing tasks, managing shifting deadlines, and driving project velocity amidst fluid mission requirements. - Superior verbal and written communication skills utilized to facilitate complex agency coordination, negotiate sensitive technical parameters, and reconcile competing priorities with production submission.

The ideal candidate is motivated by building a world-class, vertically integrated foundry from the ground up.

Hire, lead, and mentor a team of supervisors, specialists, technicians and machinists to perform blades and vanes foundry operations (core manufacturing, wax pattern, investment casting, leaching, heat treat, machining, coating, final tests and inspections, etc.)
Support factory activation, new product introductions, line expansions, and facility upgrades; contribute to strategic decision-making for foundry design and bringing the facility online
Ensure a strong focus is placed on safety and maintain an excellent safety record
Create and enforce training and career development paths to ensure timely product delivery, boost in quality, and reduction in lead time/cost
Define and enforce operational standards with strict accountability
Drive continuous improvement in manufacturing processes, procedures, quality, and rate
Collaborate with development, test, quality, and leadership to align long-term goals & resolve complex issues
Challenge requirements and legacy assumptions to establish a streamlined manufacturing environment
Ensure compliance with industry standards (e.g. ISO, AS9100, NADCAP) and SpaceX safety protocols, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, operational excellence & high-performance
Mentor and develop team members, conduct performance reviews, to maintain a world-class manufacturing organization
Own sustained CapEx, headcount, and capacity planning for foundry operations

Bachelor’s degree in engineering or STEM discipline; OR 5+ years of professional leadership experience in a manufacturing environment
5+ years of production operations or process development experience
3+ years of experience in a leadership position
